text.p: The Netherlands completed a remarkable comeback against Romania on Sunday by winning both reverse singles and qualifying for the last eight of the Davis Cup world group.
Paul Haarhuis clinched the tie by beating Romanian number two Andrei Pavel 6-3 6-1 6-2 after team mate Jan Siemerink defeated Adrian Voinea 7-6 5-7 6-7 7-6 6-4.
The Dutch, who had levelled the score in Saturday's doubles after the Romanians had taken the opening singles, did well to ignore the clamour from 6,000 boisterous Romanian fans.
Belgian umpire Michel Willems stepped in minutes before Voinea won the second set, warning the Romanians that they would be penalised if their fans continued to disturb the game.

Siemerink went on to save three match points in the fourth set when Voinea was leading 6-5 and the set score was 2-1 for Voinea. But Siemerink moved on to take a 10-8 tie-break against the Romanian, who succumbed 6-4 in the final set.

"The crucial moment was the fourth set, when I saved those three match balls. In moments like that you can only think of hanging in there. I did it. It was like winning the lottery," Siemerink, ranked 21st in the world, said.
Haarhuis, who teamed with Jacco Eltingh to win the first point for the Netherlands in Saturday's doubles, despatched Pavel in one hour and 29 minutes in Sunday's final singles.
He kept a fast speed throughout the game, also helped by strong serves. His attacks and volleys were devastating for Pavel, who had a hard time to keep pace.

"The psychological pressure was tremendous. I went from agony to ecstasy, and back again watching Voinea battle against Siemerink. When I met Haarhuis, I felt my hands and legs were missing," Pavel said.
